body.statement: Can the root-ordered sparse-core extendability handle be realized by a finite partial-support state and child map such that every live child has a globally minimal completion, children partition all completions, completed supports are never dominated by another core, and the extension test runs in \(2^{O(b\log b)}\operatorname{poly}(|V|+|E^{\mathrm{det}}|+|E^{?}|)\) time?
body.justification: This is the genuine open step: completed-support dominators are ordered, but their obligations have not been shown stable under partial extension across competing cores.
body.gap: Steiner branching supplies extension for fully selectable edge witnesses, and bounded-treewidth transversal branching supplies extension for an explicit hypergraph; neither provides this projected, implicit, cross-core extension oracle.
body.consumer: A positive resolution supplies the missing correctness and worst-delay invariant for the obstruction compiler; a negative resolution identifies the parameter that must replace \(b\).
